message.content:
Search this repository for memo-related code that computes derived metadata from memo content. I'm looking for:
1. Where metadata is computed/extracted from memo content (not user-set fields)
2. What triggers this computation (e.g., create, update operations)
3. What properties are extracted (e.g., title, snippet, tags, etc.)

Search broadly for terms like "memo", "snippet", "extract", "derive", "metadata", "computed", "content" in combination. Look at store files, service files, and any memo-related modules. Check for things like extracting a title from content, generating snippets/previews, parsing tags, etc.

Be very thorough - search across multiple naming conventions and locations.

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).

## Memo-Related Derived Metadata Computation

### 1. Core Metadata Extraction Pipeline

The central function for computing derived metadata from memo content is `RebuildMemoPayload` in `/bench/repo/server/runner/memopayload/runner.go` (line 74). It calls `markdownService.ExtractAll()` which performs a single-pass goldmark AST walk over the memo's markdown content. The markdown service is defined in `/bench/repo/internal/markdown/markdown.go`.

#### What `ExtractAll` extracts (lines 356-422 of `markdown.go`):

The `ExtractedData` struct (line 21) contains:

- **Tags** (`[]string`): All `#tag` occurrences found via custom `TagNode` AST nodes. Tags inside links/images are excluded (see `isTagNodeInLinkOrImage` at line 122). Deduplicated while preserving original case.
- **Mentions** (`[]string`): All `@mention` occurrences found via custom `MentionNode` AST nodes. Lowercased and deduplicated.
- **Property** (`*storepb.MemoPayload_Property`): A struct containing computed boolean/string properties:
  - `Title` (string): Extracted from the first block-level child of the document **only if** it is an H1 heading. Plain text is extracted recursively from the heading node (stripping inline formatting like bold/italic).
  - `HasLink` (bool): True if any `gast.KindLink` node exists.
  - `HasCode` (bool): True if any code block, fenced code block, or inline code span exists.
  - `HasTaskList` (bool): True if any GFM task checkbox exists.
  - `HasIncompleteTasks` (bool): True if any unchecked (`- [ ]`) task checkbox exists.

These properties are defined in the protobuf at `/bench/repo/proto/store/memo.proto` (the `MemoPayload.Property` message, line 15).

After `ExtractAll` returns, `RebuildMemoPayload` assigns the results to the memo's payload:
```go
memo.Payload.Tags = data.Tags
memo.Payload.Property = data.Property
```

### 2. What Triggers This Computation

**A. On Memo Create** -- `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go`, line 108:
```go
if err := memopayload.RebuildMemoPayload(ctx, create, s.MarkdownService); err != nil {
```
Called in `CreateMemo` right after building the `store.Memo` struct and before persisting it. The payload is computed and stored atomically with the memo.

**B. On Memo Update (content change)** -- `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go`, line 447:
```go
if err := memopayload.RebuildMemoPayload(ctx, memo, s.MarkdownService); err != nil {
```
Called inside `UpdateMemo` only when the `"content"` path is included in the update mask. The memo's content is updated first, then the payload is recomputed, and both are saved together.

**C. Batch Rebuild (all memos)** -- `/bench/repo/server/runner/memopayload/runner.go`, `RunOnce` method (line 27):
Iterates over all memos in batches of 100 and calls `RebuildMemoPayload` + `Store.UpdateMemo` for each. This exists as a migration/repair tool but is **not automatically invoked at server startup** (unlike the S3 presign runner). It must be called explicitly.

### 3. Snippet Generation (Computed at Read Time, Not Stored)

The `snippet` field is **not stored** in the database payload. Instead, it is computed on-the-fly every time a memo is converted to its API response format.

**Where it is computed:**

- `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_converter.go`, line 76-80: `convertMemoFromStoreWithCreators` calls `getMemoContentSnippet(memo.Content)` and sets `memoMessage.Snippet`.
- `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_webhooks.go`, line 83-90: `getMemoContentSnippet` calls `s.MarkdownService.GenerateSnippet([]byte(content), 64)` to produce a 64-character max plain-text summary.
- `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_converter.go`, lines 221-252: In `batchConvertMemoRelations`, snippets are also generated for related memos when `includeSnippets` is true.
- `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_relation_service.go`, lines 154-164: Snippets are generated for individual memo relation responses.

**How snippet generation works** (`GenerateSnippet` at markdown.go line 264):
- Walks the goldmark AST extracting plain text
- Strips code blocks (but keeps inline code span text)
- Adds spaces between block-level elements (paragraphs, headings, list items, table cells)
- Includes tag text as `#tagname`
- Includes autolink URLs
- Truncates at a word boundary if exceeding `maxLength`, appending ` ...`

### 4. Mention Extraction (Used for Notifications)

In `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_mention_helpers.go`, line 32, `ExtractAll` is called again on memo content to extract `@mentions` for notification dispatch. This happens:
- After `CreateMemo` (line 171 of `memo_service.go`)
- After `UpdateMemo` when content changes (line 511 of `memo_service.go`)

Mentions are resolved to actual users and inbox notifications are created for newly mentioned users (skipping the memo creator and previously-mentioned users on updates).

### 5. RSS Feed Title and Description (Computed at Read Time)

In `/bench/repo/server/router/rss/rss.go`:
- **Title** (line 302, `generateItemTitle`): Extracts the first line of content, strips markdown heading syntax (`#` prefixes), truncates to 100 chars at word boundary. Falls back to "Memo" if empty. This is **separate** from the `Property.Title` extraction -- it uses simple string splitting rather than AST parsing.
- **Description** (line 338, `getRSSItemDescription`): Calls `s.MarkdownService.RenderHTML(content)` to convert the full memo content to HTML.

### 6. Link Metadata (On-Demand, Not from Memo Content)

In `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_link_metadata.go`, `GetLinkMetadata` and `BatchGetLinkMetadata` fetch external URL metadata (title, description, image via OpenGraph tags) using `/bench/repo/internal/httpgetter/html_meta.go`. This is an on-demand API call, not an automatic extraction from memo content.

The service is created in `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/v1.go`, lines 48-51:
```go
markdownService := markdown.NewService(
    markdown.WithTagExtension(),
    markdown.WithMentionExtension(),
)
```
Both the tag parser and mention parser goldmark extensions are enabled. The same instance is shared with the RSS service (line 85 of `server.go`).

In `/bench/repo/proto/api/v1/memo_service.proto`, all derived fields are marked `OUTPUT_ONLY`:

- `snippet` (line 266): `string`, plain-text summary
